context.note: The line under an OPEN ask's state line on the phone, stating how stale the question is: e.g. '3 messages from you since this was asked (last 19:36)'. {count} is an integer >= 1 (the card draws no line at all for 0 or when an older runtime sends no count) and feeds the plural with `#`; {time} is an ALREADY-FORMATTED 24-hour local clock time (HH:MM) supplied by the caller — do not reformat, translate or wrap it in ICU date syntax. Both plural arms must be complete sentences because some languages reorder the parenthetical time; keep the parentheses and their wording inside each arm. It wraps onto more than one line on a narrow phone, so short words and a natural break after 'asked' are welcome.

context.note: ICU plural (RFC §2.9 digits policy: Latin numerals): the count is the raw integer of live subagents. Zero never reaches this key — format_agents returns the empty string so the segment disappears rather than reporting '0 agents'. No fixed cell cap: the band's drop ladder (drop_ladder) sheds whole segments by width.

ICU plural (RFC §2.9 digits policy: Latin numerals): the count is the raw integer of backgrounded shell jobs. Zero never reaches this key — format_jobs returns the empty string so the segment disappears. A job is a process this session started, distinct from a subagent, which is why the two counters are separate segments.

Actions count actual tool work, never incoming receipts, quiet no_reply calls or total group members. English singular is '1 action'; other counts retain 'actions'. {count} selects the locale noun form via ICU plurals; {label} is format_number(count, active_locale) for non-English locales, and the raw decimal for English. In es/fr the CLDR many branch carries no preposition after formatted digits — the guides' 'de' examples describe lexical number words such as 'un millón', not formatted numerals.
